title: Niwot Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Niwot wells have a 30-foot median depth, but fractured bedrock can make drilling cost $8,000-$15,000.
h1: Niwot, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Drilling Costs
intro_html:
Buying land or a home near Niwot means looking past the presence of a well permit. The local records show shallow wells are common, but the ground is fractured mountain bedrock, so a nearby successful well does not guarantee the same result on your property.

Within 5 miles of Niwot, Colorado DWR records include 2,297 permitted wells. Of those, 1,265 are recorded as constructed, while 1,454 report a total depth. The records are useful for setting expectations, but a site-specific driller's review, water-rights check, septic evaluation, and well inspection still matter before you close.

sections.heading: Niwot well depth: shallow records, deeper exceptions
sections.html:
The local depth median is 30 feet, and the middle half of reported wells falls between 16 and 60 feet. That is a shallow profile compared with many mountain properties. Still, the depth range is wide: 80% of wells are under 100 feet, 14% are between 100 and 300 feet, and 6% are between 300 and 600 feet. The deepest record reaches 3,000 feet.

For a bid, the median is only a starting point. Fractured granite and gneiss can change the required depth quickly when a borehole does not encounter a productive fracture. Look at nearby wells in the same geologic setting, not just the closest address. Records from Gunbarrel, Leyner, and Valmont can help provide local comparison, but they do not replace a site assessment.

sections.heading: How much water Niwot wells produce
sections.html:
Reported well yield has a 10.0 gallons-per-minute median, with the middle half between 5.0 and 15.0 gallons per minute. The largest group, 60%, reports yields from 5 to 15 gallons per minute, while 25% report more than 15 gallons per minute.

Low-producing wells are less common but important: 3% report under 1 gallon per minute, and 12% fall between 1 and 5 gallons per minute. A buyer should not treat the median as a guarantee. Ask for the well test, pump size, storage capacity, and recovery information. Household-use exempt wells generally have a 35-gallon-per-minute pumping limit, and water use still has to match the permit.

sections.heading: Niwot water levels and what the records can tell you
sections.html:
Only 80 wells in the records report a static water level, so this part of the dataset is much thinner than the depth data. Among those reports, the median depth to water is 9 feet, with the middle half between 7 and 13 feet. That suggests shallow water levels in the reported wells, but it is not enough to establish a reliable trend across every neighborhood or aquifer.

The permits identify 1,895 wells in an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer and 111 in alluvial material. They also identify 26 in the Laramie Fox Hills aquifer, while Denver Basin aquifer wells account for 28%. Confirm the aquifer and current water level for the specific parcel before relying on a neighboring measurement.

sections.heading: Niwot permit history and the drilling records
sections.html:
Niwot-area permit activity stretches from the 1950s through the newest permit year, 2025. The records show 48 permits in the 1950s, 67 in the 1960s, 259 in the 1970s, 193 in the 1980s, and 335 in the 1990s. There were 319 in the 2000s, 278 in the 2010s, and 234 in the 2020s.

The most frequent driller names in these records are Authorized (Pe, Pg), with 497 records, followed by Waneka & Son Drilling with 88 and Ground Water Systems Inc with 74. A permit record is not the same as a current inspection or performance guarantee, so verify construction, testing, and ownership documents.

sections.heading: What a new Niwot well may cost
sections.html:
The cost model for Niwot assumes fractured mountain bedrock, including granite and gneiss. Drilling is modeled at $65 to $100 per foot. At the local 30-foot median depth, the drilled hole alone works out to about $2,000 to $3,000.

That is not the complete project price. A finished well with a pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical work is modeled at about $8,000 to $15,000. A deeper hole, difficult access, casing and grout requirements, or a low-yield result can change the bid. Have the contractor separate drilling, casing, pump equipment, electrical, trenching, testing, and any failed-hole provisions so you can compare bids accurately.

sections.heading: Niwot risks to check before buying or building
sections.html:
Water quality deserves a parcel-specific review. Within about 10 miles, the map shows 470 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 115 historic mine features, and 17 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Those mapped sites do not prove contamination at your property, but they are a reason to test the well water and review nearby land uses, direction of groundwater flow, and the well's construction.

Also check for low yield, dry-hole history, damaged casing or grout, and adequate separation between the well and septic system. A new home may require an augmentation plan in an over-appropriated basin. Confirm the permit's allowed use, domestic limits, septic feasibility, driveway access, and building envelope before buying land or starting design.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Niwot, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within five miles of Niwot is 30 feet, and the middle half runs from 16 to 60 feet. Most, 80%, are under 100 feet. Conditions vary sharply in fractured granite and gneiss, however; 6% are between 300 and 600 feet, and the deepest record is 3,000 feet.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Niwot?
faq.a: The local cost model uses $65 to $100 per foot for fractured mountain bedrock. At the 30-foot median depth, drilling the hole is estimated at about $2,000 to $3,000. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical work is modeled at $8,000 to $15,000, before unusual access or deeper drilling changes the price.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Niwot?
faq.a: Reported yields have a 10.0-gallon-per-minute median, with the middle half from 5.0 to 15.0 gallons per minute. Sixty percent report between 5 and 15 gallons per minute. Low-yield wells still occur: 3% report under 1 gallon per minute and 12% report from 1 to 5 gallons per minute.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Niwot?
faq.a: The well records cannot establish drinking-water safety. Mapped sites within about 10 miles include 470 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 115 historic mine features, and 17 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Test the specific well for appropriate contaminants, inspect its casing and grout, and review nearby land uses before relying on the water.

faq.q: Can I build a home on a well near Niwot?
faq.a: Possibly, but the permit and site need review. Confirm the well's permitted use, yield, pump equipment, septic layout, and water-quality results. Domestic and household wells make up 42% of the recorded use mix. If the basin is over-appropriated, an augmentation plan may be required. A Colorado DWR and county review should happen before purchase or construction.
